subject: earth-science
intro: Earth science leads to reading and managing the planet — mapping resources, tracing water, assessing hazards and advising on the energy and environmental decisions societies face.

roles.title: Geoscientists, Except Hydrologists and Geographers
roles.what: Study the composition, structure and physical processes of the Earth — exploring for oil, gas, minerals and underground water, and working on waste disposal, land reclamation and other environmental problems.
roles.where: Plate tectonics (unit 2), minerals (unit 3) and geologic time (unit 7), with the earthquakes-and-seismology lessons, are the core toolkit geoscientists apply in field and subsurface work.

roles.title: Hydrologists
roles.what: Research how underground and surface waters are distributed and move — precipitation, infiltration, groundwater flow and return to the ocean — to manage supplies, floods and contamination.
roles.where: Unit 11, Water — the water cycle, streams and drainage basins, flooding, groundwater and aquifers — plus the coastlines chapters on tides and currents, is this career's daily subject matter.

roles.title: Mining and Geological Engineers, Including Mining Safety Engineers
roles.what: Survey potential mining and construction sites, design safe and economical extraction and ground-support systems, and inspect for unsafe geological conditions while coordinating mine safety programmes.
roles.where: Energy and mineral resources (unit 16) — mining and ore formation — with igneous processes (unit 4) and crustal deformation and earthquakes (unit 9) teach the ore-deposit and rock-mechanics thinking involved.

roles.title: Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
roles.what: Identify, investigate and help eliminate sources of pollution and hazards that affect the environment or public health, working from measurements and observations of air, water, soil and food.
roles.where: Global climate change (unit 15) and the greenhouse-effect and carbon-cycle lessons, with weathering, erosion and landforms (unit 5), train this pollutant-tracing, evidence-based stance.

roles.title: Geological Technicians, Except Hydrologic Technicians
roles.what: Support scientists and engineers with electronic, sonic and nuclear measuring instruments in laboratory, exploration and production work — analysing drill cuttings and logging well pressures and temperatures.
roles.where: Mineral identification (unit 3), rock classification (units 4 to 6) and the fossils-and-geologic-time lessons give the hand-specimen and sampling skills technicians use daily.
